# Standard library and globals allowlist

<!-- Generated by tooling/manifest/build-stdlib.mjs from compiler/profile/stdlib.source.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Closed-world, default-deny list of the built-ins the compiler may reference and the runtime must provide (WP-G0E; design rows L18 and L21).
Anything not listed is unsupported. X and E entries, and unknown names, fail with a diagnostic. The lookup API is `compiler/profile/stdlib.mjs`, also re-exported from `compiler/profile/index.mjs`.

Status letters: **P** faithful, **A** adaptation, **W** web-only (no entries), **X** excluded (must fail), **E** experimental (not promised). Targets: `native`, `web` and `test`. A P or A entry is supported on each target it lists.

Regenerate with `node tooling/manifest/build-stdlib.mjs`; check with `node tooling/manifest/build-stdlib.mjs --check`.

## Decisions

1. Status letters follow design.md section 8 and compiler/profile/index.mjs. P and A are supported on native and web. W is supported only on web. X, E and unknown names are never supported.
2. Shared entries list all three targets, because the test target runs the same builtins. trace and testHost list only the test target.
3. No W entries. Browser globals are X on both targets. Design S23 permits web imports only in an explicit extension, and design section 11 carries networking, timers and storage as services. C1a VN4011 applies to native only; the coordinator decides whether a web list is wanted.
4. globalThis is X (VN4013, L20), not P as WP-G0E listed it. WP-B1 still installs it for the runtime, so the later diff test must accept declared X entries. A reachable global object would bypass static path checks.
5. Intl and RegExp are E, following design L18 (broad parity E). Date (constructor, parse, UTC and every instance method) is E, and Date.now is A. WP-G0E listed Date, Intl and RegExp with the X entries; the coordinator kept them E. Instance members of Intl and RegExp are not enumerated, so they are unsupported.
6. ArrayBuffer and Uint8Array are P (coordinator decision; design L18 bytes for IO): the constructors, the statics and the members the coordinator listed. Uint8Array members are listed under Uint8Array.prototype, although %TypedArray%.prototype defines them, because that is what users reach. Element indexing is syntax and has no entry. No builtin WP implements typed arrays yet, so these entries are plans.
7. Other typed arrays, DataView, SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics are X (design L18: X until inventoried; VN4014 for typed arrays and DataView).
8. Math.random, Date.now and performance.now are A (coordinator decision; host providers under design L19): seeded and deterministic in tests, never used for secrets. performance is A only so that performance.now resolves. manifest.json (WP-G0B) lists Math.random and Date.now as A, so the two manifests agree.
9. Promise and the Error types are P as listed (coordinator decision). WP-B5 will implement them. Error name and message, Error#cause and AggregateError#errors are also P.
10. Kinds are the six in WP-G0E plus prop, for instance-own properties that a built-in creates (Error#cause, AggregateError#errors). Path forms: Ctor.prototype.name, Ctor.prototype[Symbol.x], Ctor#prop for instance properties, and %Intrinsic%.name for intrinsic objects that user code cannot name. memberPath never produces a % or # path.
11. Paths are unique across kinds, so isStdlibSupported(path, target) needs no kind.
12. A P or A entry cites a design row whose status set contains that status (the WP-G0B rule; L05 and L20 are X-only, L19 is A-only). X and E entries may cite any row. Where no row names the replacement service, an entry cites L21 (default-deny governance). Clock, timer and test-provider entries cite L19.
13. X entries carry a user-facing hint. Entries that C1a already reports carry its VN code: VN4001 to VN4011, VN4013 to VN4015, and VN2017 for __proto__ access. Object.defineProperty, Object.defineProperties and Object.setPrototypeOf map to VN4008.
14. Overloads are not listed separately. Object.create is P with a note: only an undefined properties argument is supported. L21 asks for overload-level entries, so this is an open question.
15. Left out, so unsupported by default: Error#stack (design L13 names a source stack but does not say whether error.stack is an API; open question), Set.prototype[Symbol.toStringTag] (WP-B4 does not list it, but V8 has it; open question), Promise.prototype[Symbol.toStringTag], and every method that no B-spec or WP-G0E names.
16. Promise.try is X. It is not in WP-G0E, but users reach for it.
17. Locale-dependent methods (toLocaleString, localeCompare, toLocaleUpperCase, toLocaleLowerCase, and toLocaleString on arrays) are X. WP-B3 marks them NO, and design L19 makes locale a platform service.
18. trace and testHost are A on the test target only, row L19 (seeded test provider). Source: docs/dev/trace-format.md.
19. TextEncoder and TextDecoder (constructors and instance members) are A: a platform-provided UTF-8 codec. L19 is the only design row with status A among the L rows, so they cite L19; the bytes they handle are design L18 bytes for IO.
20. globalThis stays X for user code (C1a VN4013, L20). The runtime still installs it through WP-B1, so the diff test accepts declared X entries.
